findings.proposed: (unchanged) — this locale's two-target render is number-neutral and correct; the upstream cardinality fix is the renderer's
findings.detail: A consent roll-up (two records sharing one request_id — the grouping key team-bridge-member-events-model.ts:144-156 groups on) produces one line with two targets, and the owner arm renders the possessive singular over the pair: « Sana Ketabchi已同意自己的智能体Aida (Sana Ketabchi)和Scout (Sana Ketabchi)加入 » — Chinese does not mark grammatical number, so this reads correctly. English has the same defect ("their agent A and B"), so this is not a translation error: the sentence's grammatical number depends on a cardinality nothing enforces, and the en sidecar's "always exactly one name for this key" is that unenforced assumption. No local change follows: the only defect on the two-target path is upstream. Reachability: the UI merges these events itself; whether the hub emits two consent records under one request_id is unverified (the server is not deployed and no corpus is readable here).

findings.proposed: if (line.actor.kind !== "human") return false;  /* before the every() test; the cardinality guard is CO-B1 */
findings.detail: The predicate compares account ids but never the actor's kind. An agent party carries its OWNER's account_id (the contract's own statement, restated in the model's docstring), so a consent whose actor is an agent on the same account takes the owner arm and the sentence claims a relation an agent cannot have. Executed: actor = agent "Aida (Sana Ketabchi)", target = agent "Scout (Sana Ketabchi)" renders Aida (Sana Ketabchi)已同意自己的智能体Scout (Sana Ketabchi)加入 — for this locale the self-approval reading the audit was asked about becomes possible only through this hole, never through the wording. Minor: no readable corpus proves the hub records an agent as the consenting actor; the guard costs one line and makes the predicate match its own docstring ("the actor owns the target").
